thumbnail.relationship_to_result: deterministic size-only resampling of render.png for thumbnail inspection; not a second generation or a content edit

gates.description: Live trees visibly vary in trunk diameter and height rather than forming one uniform cohort.
gates.observable_evidence: At 384 x 256, massive edge trunks, several medium-diameter conifers, and slender saplings differ clearly in both girth and height across the frame.

gates.description: Overstory, midstory, and understory remain spatially separate across the forest depth.
gates.observable_evidence: Both views separate foreground ferns and low broadleaf growth, middle-distance saplings and conifer boughs, and tall overstory crowns surrounding the bright canopy opening.

gates.description: A standing dead snag is visibly distinct from shadowed or leafless live trunks.
gates.observable_evidence: The center-frame upright snag has a jagged broken crown, exposed weathered brown wood, and no live crown, making it structurally distinct from the surrounding green live conifers.

gates.description: A large fallen log has credible scale and physical contact with the forest floor.
gates.observable_evidence: A person-scaled, moss-covered decaying trunk spans the lower-left foreground and rests through wet vegetation; additional downed trunks lie along the right floor, all readable at both scales.

gates.description: Uniform plantation rows, generic lushness, or a single giant tree do not substitute for the complete structure.
gates.observable_evidence: The thumbnail simultaneously shows irregularly spaced multi-size live cohorts, separated vegetation tiers, a central snag, and several fallen logs; it is not a row plantation, generic green wall, or single-tree scene.

gates.description: One concrete saved image is reviewed at thumbnail and native scale; no cross-attempt component averaging is allowed.
gates.observable_evidence: The native result is one saved PNG with SHA-256 20d4c269617b06545aeb837fec50a488ccfa87634791766fbefd239dcb60d0b2; the thumbnail is only a size-resampled inspection view of those same pixels.

gates.description: The assigned environmental system remains the dominant readable scene structure rather than a decorative backdrop behind a portrait.
gates.observable_evidence: At thumbnail scale the forest spans the full frame and its logs, trunks, snag, and crown tiers establish the composition; the crouching observer is a small subordinate figure near the lower center-right.

gates.description: An unmistakably adult subject shows general facial-appearance and long dark softly waved hair continuity with the attached reference without making a same-person or identity claim.
gates.observable_evidence: The rendered subject is visibly adult and has long dark softly waved hair, but the face is tiny at thumbnail scale and remains a downward-looking three-quarter profile at native scale. General facial-appearance continuity with the frontal reference cannot be observed confidently at both required scales; hair continuity alone is only partial evidence.

gates.description: The reference-guided subject is integrated into the scene without hiding any required environmental component or relation.
gates.observable_evidence: The observer remains small and low in the frame; the central snag, main fallen log, different live-tree cohorts, and foreground-to-crown layering remain readable around the figure at both scales.

gates.description: Perspective lighting anatomy material contact and scale read as one coherent photorealistic capture.
gates.observable_evidence: Native inspection shows a consistent wide-angle perspective, mist-softened daylight, coherent wet bark and moss, credible tree-to-human scale, and plausible crouching anatomy, camera grip, and ground contact.

verdict_reason: The protocol requires all five target gates and all five shared gates to pass in the same saved image. Facial-appearance continuity is not observable at both required scales, so partial hair continuity cannot qualify the image.

review_audit.reason: audit_image_render_review.py audits only a frozen generic render-repair contract. This initial v6 candidate pack has no render_repair contract; the coordinator target and shared gates are recorded directly here.

boundary: These are direct pixel observations, not identity claims or user preference. Prompt and runtime audit success did not determine the pixel verdict.
